# pflow.xyz — Petri net editor, simulator, and browser math library

pflow.xyz is a visual Petri net editor with an embeddable, dependency-free ES
module library for discrete simulation and continuous (ODE) analysis. All
modules are served from this origin with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so
they can be imported directly from any ad-hoc HTML page — no build step, no
npm.

## Modules (import these URLs directly)

- https://pflow.xyz/petri-solver.js — mass-action ODE solver (Tsit5, adaptive)
  plus SVGPlotter, an interactive SVG line/scatter plotter.
  Exports: fromJSON, setState, setRates, ODEProblem, ODESolution, Tsit5,
  solve, SVGPlotter, Place, Transition, Arc, PetriNet.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-sim.js — discrete firing semantics (pure functions).
  Exports: enabled, fire, enabledTransitions, marking, getArcWeight,
  capacityOf.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-colors.js — colored-net unfolding (expandColors,
  expandState). petri-solver.js imports it automatically.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.js — the full `<petri-view>` editor web
  component (drag-and-drop editing, discrete play mode, tabbed Analysis
  workbench: ODE simulate / rate scan / sweep / phase plot).
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.css — editor styles (design tokens, light +
  dark via prefers-color-scheme).
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-learn.js — differentiable fitting for Petri-net ODE
  models: a JS mirror of go-pflow's `learn` package. Forward sensitivities
  (`LearnableProblem.solveWithSensitivities`, augmented ODE with analytic
  Jacobian) and reverse-mode/adjoint sensitivities
  (`LearnableProblem.solveAdjoint`, one backward solve — the tool for a rate
  function with many parameters, at a cost independent of parameter count).
  Exports: `LearnableProblem`, `ScalarRateFunc`, `SharedScalar` (tied
  parameters), `mseLossGrad`/`relativeMseLossGrad`/`mseLossAdjoint`/
  `relativeMseLossAdjoint`, `adamMinimize`/`nelderMead`/`coordinateDescent`,
  `hingeRankLoss`, `fit`/`fitGradient`/`fitRates` (the no-boilerplate
  entry point: fit per-transition scalar rates to observed trajectories).
  petri-solver.js's bytes are untouched by this module.
- https://pflow.xyz/petri-ssa.js — portable Gillespie SSA (discrete-stochastic
  simulation), byte-exact with go-pflow, pflow-rs and pflow-jl via a fixed
  PRNG (SplitMix64 → xoshiro256**) and a ported log; no dependency on the
  other modules. `simulate(model, {horizon, samples, realizations, seed})` →
  `{ places, times, series: {id: {values, stddev}}, final }` (ensemble
  mean/stddev/final per place). Exports: splitmix64, Xoshiro256, plog,
  combinations, compile, simulate.

The ODE semantics are behaviorally identical to go-pflow
(github.com/pflow-xyz/go-pflow) — enforced by a differential parity test
suite — so browser results match server-side analysis.

## Model format (JSON-LD)

```json
{
  "@context": "https://pflow.xyz/schema",
  "@type": "PetriNet",
  "@version": "1.1",
  "token": ["https://pflow.xyz/tokens/black"],
  "places": {
    "water":  { "@type": "Place", "initial": [10], "capacity": [0], "x": 60,  "y": 60 },
    "coffee": { "@type": "Place", "initial": [0],  "capacity": [0], "x": 260, "y": 60 }
  },
  "transitions": {
    "brew": { "@type": "Transition", "x": 160, "y": 60 }
  },
  "arcs": [
    { "@type": "Arrow", "source": "water", "target": "brew", "weight": [1] },
    { "@type": "Arrow", "source": "brew", "target": "coffee", "weight": [1] }
  ]
}
```

Notes: `capacity` 0 or absent means unbounded. `initial`, `capacity`, and
`weight` are vectors — one entry per token color in `token`; an explicit 0
weight component means "this color is not involved". Set
`"inhibitTransition": true` on an arc for an inhibitor.

## Sandboxed environments (strict-CSP hosts)

**claude.ai artifacts cannot load these modules today.** Artifact CSP allows
external scripts only from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`; imports from pflow.xyz,
jsDelivr, esm.sh, or unpkg are all refused there and fail with
`Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`. Don't write a fallback loader
for artifacts — it fails on every origin. Host the page elsewhere (any static
host works; the modules are CORS-open). A cdnjs submission is staged; once
accepted, `https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/pflow-xyz/<version>/petri-solver.js`
will be the artifact-compatible URL — until then that URL 404s.

Also: `file://` pages can't load ES modules at all (CORS blocks them), so
"open the HTML file in a browser" is not enough for local use — serve it,
e.g. `python3 -m http.server`.

For *other* strict-CSP hosts that do allow common CDNs, jsDelivr mirrors the
repo; relative imports (petri-colors.js) resolve against whichever origin
loaded the module, so either source is self-sufficient:

```js
const pf = await import("https://pflow.xyz/petri-solver.js")
  .catch(() => import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@v1.26.0/public/petri-solver.js"));
```

Pin a release tag (as above) or commit SHA — `@main` is cached ~12h by
jsDelivr, so it lags the latest deploy. `@pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz` has been on npm
since 2026-08-01, so npm-backed CDNs work too:
`https://esm.sh/@pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@1.26.0/petri-solver.js` or
`https://unpkg.com/@pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@1.26.0/petri-solver.js` (same paths
work for petri-learn.js, petri-sim.js, etc. — see package.json's `exports`
map). cdnjs listing is pending (needs 800+ npm downloads/month or 200 GitHub
stars).

## Minimal ad-hoc page: solve an ODE and plot it

```html
<div id="plot"></div>
<script type="module">
  const pf = await import("https://pflow.xyz/petri-solver.js")
    .catch(() => import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/pflow-xyz/pflow-xyz@v1.26.0/public/petri-solver.js"));

  const model = { /* JSON-LD model as above */ };
  const net = pf.fromJSON(model);
  const prob = new pf.ODEProblem(net, pf.setState(net), [0, 10],
                                 pf.setRates(net, { brew: 0.5 }));
  const sol = pf.solve(prob, pf.Tsit5(), { dt: 0.01, abstol: 1e-6, reltol: 1e-3, adaptive: true });

  const plot = pf.SVGPlotter.plotSolution(sol, ["water", "coffee"], {
    title: "Brew kinetics", xlabel: "Time", ylabel: "Tokens", width: 720, height: 400,
  });
  document.getElementById("plot").innerHTML = plot.svg;
  plot.setupInteractivity();   // crosshair, tooltip, click-to-toggle legend
  console.log(sol.getFinalState());
</script>
```

The emitted SVG uses `var(--pv-viz-*, lightFallback)` colors: it renders the
validated light palette standalone, and follows the host theme if the page
defines those custom properties (petri-view.css does).

## Minimal ad-hoc page: full editor

```html
<script type="module" src="https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://pflow.xyz/petri-view.css">
<petri-view data-json-editor>
  <script type="application/ld+json">{ /* JSON-LD model */ }</script>
</petri-view>
```

## Discrete simulation

```js
import * as sim from "https://pflow.xyz/petri-sim.js";
sim.enabledTransitions(model);        // -> ["brew"]
const marks = sim.fire(model, "brew"); // -> {"water":[9],"coffee":[1]} or null
```

`fire` is pure: pass the returned marking back as the third argument to step
again.

## Related services

- POST https://pflow.xyz/api/svg — render a model to SVG server-side.
- GET  https://pflow.xyz/schema — the JSON-LD @context.
- https://pilot.pflow.xyz/mcp — petri-pilot MCP server (JSON-RPC): the same
  math as tools (petri_ode, petri_rate_scan, petri_ode_sweep,
  petri_phase_plot, petri_stochastic, petri_fit, petri_optimize, …) plus
  validation, verification, and full-stack code generation. It accepts a flat
  model format: `{"name": "...", "places": [{"id","initial"}],
  "transitions": [{"id"}], "arcs": [{"from","to","weight"}]}`. The editor's
  Analysis dialog has a "Copy MCP call" button that emits ready-to-send
  payloads.
- https://book.pflow.xyz — the book on modeling with Petri nets.
